result_text:
`all_files.zip` now packages the scope file lists by the names they were written under, so renaming an aspect no longer breaks the export. The change is in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, in the zip-export block.

The five scope entries used to be hard-coded literals like `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`. Renaming the aspect to `buildAndDeployment` made the read of that file throw. The surrounding `catch (Throwable)` swallowed it, which is why `all_files.zip` and `git-history.zip` were both skipped.

The code now loops over the five scope aspects in the same order as before. For each one it gets the name from `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same call that writes the loose files, and reads that file for the zip entry. With the default config the entries stay `aspect_main.txt`, `aspect_test.txt`, `aspect_generated.txt`, `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`, `aspect_other.txt`.

The `reports` module compiles and its one existing test (`ReportFileExporterTest`) passes. I did not run the renamed-aspect scenario end to end, and no test covers this export. I also did not change the broad `catch (Throwable)`, so any other failure in that block is still only logged.
